questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: University of Helsinki has an excellent Aleksanteri Institute, which the center of advanced Russian studies

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The reason why I put 9 instead of 10 is that even though I enjoyed my stay, Helsinki is a really expensive city, so I came with a minus on my bank account. Even the Erasmus Grant couldn't fully cover the expenses. So I would recommend Helsinki to people, but will warn them about the costs.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. The University of Helsinki had sent several newsletters, which were very helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Tutors and orientation week with all information needed for exchange students

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was a pretty calm process to find the accommodation. The University of Helsinki provided me with one, where I should fill out the form whether I want to live with University's companies HOAS or Unihome, and whether I want to live alone or with other students.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Prepare to live 45 minutes away from the city center.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall, I'm satisfied with the university's assistance regarding accommodations.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was quite challenging to figure out how their system SISU, is functioning. It doesn't have user-friendly software, and sometimes, even if you register in advance and fulfill the requirements for the course, you still have a risk to be kicked out of the course for no reason.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Only guidance how to use SISU in the orientation week. Otherwise, if I had a problem, I had to contact the teacher of the course.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
70% out of 100%
Even when a course was in English, but was not open for exchange students, I had to fight for the right to being registered in the course by convincing the administration. Luckily, they were very quick to response and help me with the process. 
Otherwise I've been rejected an access to one course, but I didn't get a satisfactory information what I have to do in this situation.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Prepare yourself for not getting the courses you want,  therefore ask the services what to do in the situation, when the course is not available.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I put 4 instead of 5, because of one

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: All six courses were at the MA level, which required a lot of reading, projects, essays etc

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
It depends. I was surprised to experience that some of my teachers used creative methods to help us memorize stuff. 
I also appreciated that the teachers came up with the questions or detailed description on the task, which we could use for writing our essays. The University of Copenhagen is unfortunately way back in that matter. Teachers expect from us that we can figure out ourselves, but didn't even get guidance on how to make a good question for research. We had to figure ourselves out, which is a totally stressful process. If you are going to use this feedback for the improvement of our education system in Denmark, please convince the teachers to come up with meta questions, which could be a good start for finding your own question. Not only for BA-level, but for MA-level as well.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Russian legal system and law
- Interactions and responses
- EU human rights
- Land question and sustainable development 
- China and Russia in Central Asia 
- Qualitative Interview Method in Sociology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
- Russian legal system and law
Because you get exclusive insight perspective on Russian legal system. The teacher, Marianna Muravyeva, is the best
- EU human rights
It gives a post-structural perspective on EU

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and accomodation are more expensive here. It is cheaper to eat in canteens (22 DKK per meal) than buying in supermarkets.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Very strong Student Union and very active student organisations.
Copenhagen needs to keep up!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Evert kind: sport, political, study related, festivals, cultural events for students from humanities, cultural events for every student in Helsinki.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
First of all, there are a lot of opportunities, and sometimes you feel that it is overwhelming to catch up on all of them. So, therefore I would recommend to contact the student organisation, which is related to your study track. Fx Russian and Eastern European Studies have Sasha organisation, where they arrange movie nights, draw-along with Bob-Ross etc. There you can meet people, who share the same interest as you. 
It's good to join UniSport, a sport student organisation. Sport is good for the health and soul, and they have sauna. I didn't join the organisation though. I had already major expenses.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Many cinemas in Helsinki have English subtitles, so foreigners can enjoy movies, too. 
A lot of museums have free entrance days.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: A bit challenging. Finns are very social people at first glance

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join a student organisation. Finns will be forced to speak to you, and you get friends out of it

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
Social awkwardness
Cold and dry climate (buy thermo clothes and a lot of cream!)
Dark humour
Finnish students work way more than Danish students, they are quite stressed.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
I really liked that the administration and teachers responded to me right away or the next day. Unfortunately, the University of Copenhagen is way back in that sense
Saunas
The universities in Finland take care of the students; canteens and student accommodations get subsidies from the government.
Respect for one's personal space. Even if it's crowded, you feel that you have a space for yourself. I don't experience it here in CPH
Beautiful language, actually

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Prepare for extra expenses
- Join a student organisation and other student cultural events, like Independence Day or the 1st of May. This is where you can experience the real student life in Finland.
- It's okay to feel alone

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not what I can think of right now

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
New acquittances
Perspective on the Nordic country, which is quite ignored in Denmark, I think.
New insights into Russian and Eastern European Studies

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Keeping up with a lot of essays. It's hard, but you learn a lot by using the materials in written form

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Not what I can think of

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
